title: Tech Note: 4D Server Licensing: Tips and Troubleshooting

historical_commentary.text: Only the teaser survives for this note, which covers how 4D Client connections consume 4D Server licenses and how to troubleshoot failed connections. The general concept of concurrent-user licensing and connection troubleshooting persists today, but the specific licensing mechanics of 1997-era 4D Server (dongle/serial-based user-count licenses) are dated relative to 4D's modern licensing model.
related_updates: 4D's licensing model and license-management tooling have changed substantially since the 1990s (e.g. modern license center/online activation vs. era-appropriate physical/serial-based licensing)
Client-to-server connection protocols have also evolved considerably since 1997 (TCP/IP now standard, legacy AppleTalk/IPX transports long discontinued)
